items.title: These 3 Dividend ETFs Own Nvidia and Microsoft and Still Pay Up to 8 Percent
items.summary: Owning Nvidia and Microsoft while collecting a fat dividend income used to mean picking one or the other. A new generation of ETFs rewrites that tradeoff in three very different ways, and the mechanics behind each one matter before you buy.

items.title: Marvell Technology Is Betting More Of Its Revenue On One End Market
items.summary: Three-quarters of its sales already come from data centers, and the company's own guidance widens that share even as it plans for cloud spending growth to cool.

items.title: The 5 Best Long-Term Investment Stocks to Buy for Steady Returns
items.summary: The best long-term investment stocks are built on strong brands, balance sheets and cash flow, and they pay reliable dividends that grow over time.

items.title: AMD is Down 10% Over a Month: Did Microsoft’s Catalyst Just Spark the 155% Upside Expected By Wall Street Pro?
items.summary: Baird just set the highest AMD price target on Wall Street after a brutal July selloff, and a surprise Microsoft announcement may have handed AMD the exact catalyst needed to justify it.

items.title: Should You Buy AMD Stock Ahead of Q2 Earnings? Here's What to Know
items.summary: AMD heads into Q2 earnings with robust EPYC, Instinct and Ryzen AI demand, but a lofty valuation and fierce competition temper its growth outlook.

items.title: Broadcom No Longer Sells Itself As A Chip Cycle Story
items.summary: The business management once framed around a cyclical bottom is still growing, but it now gets a paragraph while artificial intelligence gets the company.

items.title: Qualcomm Stock's Biggest Risk Is The Gap Between Pain And Payoff
items.summary: Just over half of revenue still leans on a shrinking handset market, and the businesses meant to replace it do not reach their targeted scale for years.

items.title: Marvell Down Huge This Month: The Pros See 120% Returns in 12 Months
items.summary: Marvell collapsed 32% in a single month while 44 analysts refused to cut their targets, leaving a widening gap between where the stock trades and where the Street thinks it belongs.
